obraz: The door swollen by rain opens at the third push of your shoulder.
proc: Resistance gives way to bodily force of the shoulder.
Resistance yields to bodily force.

obraz: After months of practice, you answer in the new language without translating first.
proc: Long earlier practice ripens into a result that could not be hurried.
Long earlier work ripens into a result that could not be hurried.

obraz: The potato forgotten in the cupboard has put out white shoots.
proc: Unseen in the closed cupboard something completed itself and sprouted.
Closed away and unwatched, it has grown from within.

obraz: The rowan feeds the thrush, and the thrush carries its seed over the hill.
proc: What is given and carried on spreads and grows; an exchange between two.
Each side gives the other something in an uncounted exchange.

obraz: You turn down the praise and say whose work it was.
proc: Keeps to the truth and gives up the praise knowingly.
You keep to the truth and knowingly give up the praise.

obraz: The reply is written in a single breath, and your thumb stops above the send button.
proc: A stop just before the rushed move is made.
A rushed move is stopped just before it is made.

obraz: The coins dropped in the jar each evening are, one day, the fare.
proc: Small deeds over time show as a result one day.
Small acts done long before show one day as a result.

obraz: The recipe card is in another hand, with one change added in yours.
proc: Something handed down, carried on with one's own change.
Something inherited is carried on with one's own choice added.

obraz: Halfway through the dishes a song comes on, and you both join in.
proc: Shared joy in the middle of a task.
Shared joy arrives in the middle of a chore.

obraz: The child struggles with the zip, and you wait while they try again.
proc: Fragile growing ability is given room rather than forced.
A small one is given room to grow rather than forced.

obraz: The cold of the river at your ankles stops you before the current does.
proc: A sharp sensation stops the step before the danger is reached.
A sharp sensation stops the step at the edge before the danger.

obraz: The umbrella turns inside out in the gust; you push it back and walk on.
proc: Outside gust breaks the thing; it is righted and one goes on.
An outside gust breaks the umbrella's shape, and you see it still serves.

obraz: The table has moved through three homes and still stands in the kitchen.
proc: A thing carried through homes and kept; it endures the changes.
A thing carried on from home to home.

obraz: Dinner is burnt, and the table laughs over bread and cheese.
proc: Joy shared in the middle of a failed plan.
Shared laughter in the middle of a mishap, not a reward.

obraz: The seedling droops for a week in its new pot, then puts out one leaf.
proc: Fragile new life given room puts out a first leaf after strain.
Fragile new growth appears after being given time and room.

obraz: Your foot is already off the kerb when the horn sounds.
proc: A sound stops the move at the threshold of the kerb.
A sharp stop comes right at the threshold of a move.

obraz: The tall grass lies flat in the wind and is standing again by evening.
proc: Bends under strain and does not break.
It bends under strain and does not break.

obraz: The stream runs in the bed the old river cut.
proc: The new runs in the course inherited from the old.
The new follows a course handed down by what came before.

obraz: On the first warm day every door on the street stands open.
proc: A shared lightening moment as the warmth comes.
A shared lightening as everything opens at once.

obraz: The eider plucks her own down to line the nest.
proc: Care preparing room for new small life, at her own cost.
Care prepares a soft place for fragile new life.

obraz: One person says the name no one has said all evening, and the table goes quiet.
proc: A spoken name arrives and changes the room.
A spoken name arrives and changes the whole table.

obraz: The runner slows to a walk on the hill and does not stop.
proc: Endures the strain, yielding in pace but not breaking off.
Under strain the runner yields pace but does not break off.

obraz: You read the same message again in the morning, and it says something else.
proc: After the turn from night to morning the same thing reads differently.
After night turns to morning the same thing reads differently.

obraz: The flight is cancelled at the gate, and the queue turns round as one.
proc: Outside force breaks the plan.
An outside event breaks the plan for everyone at once.

obraz: Two people walk side by side, and neither could say who set the pace.
proc: Two share a rhythm that neither imposed.
Two share one pace that neither imposed.

obraz: Said aloud, the plan sounds different from the one in your head.
proc: Spoken aloud, the word changes the meaning of the thing.
Speaking it aloud changes what the thing means.

obraz: A parcel sits on the step, taped shut, with no sender's name.
proc: A closed vessel with contents that exist but are not yet known.
A closed vessel whose contents exist but are unknown.

obraz: You turn the map on your phone, and the street falls into place.
proc: Things fall into place after a turn; view shifts.
One turn and the same scene suddenly reads right.

obraz: A power cut ends the video call and takes the unsaved slide with it.
proc: Uninvited outside force breaks things and shows what is lost.
An outside force cuts the plan and shows what was lost.

obraz: Two people carry a long mirror through the doorway, one pausing as the other turns.
proc: Two move one load by adjusting to each other.
Two move a load only by matching each other's rhythm.

obraz: The raven calls once from the roof, and everyone at the door looks up.
proc: A sound arrives and changes everyone's attention.
A single sound arrives and turns everyone's attention.

obraz: An unnamed voice memo sits in your phone, three minutes long.
proc: Something exists, unnamed and not yet heard.
Content exists but is not yet known or opened.

obraz: The tide has turned, and the same boats now point the other way.
proc: A turn after which the same things stand the other way.
A turn after which the same things face the other way.

obraz: One minute of hail, and the tulips are lying on the path.
proc: Hail from outside breaks what stood.
An uninvited force from outside flattens what stood.

obraz: Two swans cross the lake, and the gap between them never changes.
proc: Two move together in an unchanging common rhythm.
Two move together in a steady common rhythm.

obraz: The path across the grass is on no plan; it is where everyone actually walks.
proc: A road made by going.
A road made simply by people walking it.

obraz: The tide pool at dusk moves once, and whatever moved does not show itself.
proc: Something moves under the surface, sensed but not seen.
Something stirs under the surface and stays unseen.

obraz: A new document is open, and the cursor blinks on the first line.
proc: An open unwritten space.
An empty page with nothing written yet.

obraz: The phone is at two per cent, and you send the one message that matters.
proc: Scarcity shows what is truly needed.
Scarcity forces the choice of the one thing truly needed.

obraz: You hear your own phrase come out of a friend's mouth and learn how it sounds.
proc: One learns about oneself through another, as a mirror.
You learn about yourself by hearing it from another.

obraz: On the long drive you miss your turning because the road was so easy to follow.
proc: The rhythm of the road carries one past where one meant to go.
The rhythm of the road carries you past where you meant to go.

obraz: The door opens on its chain, just far enough to see who is knocking.
proc: Guarded opening: open to the world yet not letting everything in.
A guarded opening that lets one look without letting all in.

obraz: One wall in the new flat is still bare, without a single nail hole.
proc: Unmarked surface where nothing has been set yet.
An unmarked space where nothing has been put yet.

obraz: One seat is left on the last bus, and two of you are still on the pavement.
proc: Not enough for both; constraint presses.
There is not enough for both, and the lack presses.

obraz: A friend copies the way you tap your foot, and you had never noticed it.
proc: One sees oneself through another's mirroring.
You see your own habit through another person.

obraz: After the first hour of walking your feet stop asking how far it is.
proc: Rhythm found only by moving.
A rhythm is found only by walking.

obraz: The phone is silenced for the night, with three numbers allowed to ring through.
proc: A guard that lets only some through.
A guard that stays open to a few and keeps the rest out.

obraz: Fresh snow lies on the field, and nothing has crossed it yet.
proc: Unmarked field with no sign on it yet.
An unmarked surface with no trace written yet.

obraz: The birch on the lava field grows no taller than the rock that shelters it.
proc: Growth limited by constraint to what the shelter allows.
The rock stands between the threat and the tree, which lives only within that shelter.

obraz: In the dark window of the train your own face sits among the other passengers.
proc: One's own face seen among others, in a mirror.
You see yourself among other people, as in a mirror.

obraz: The phone light finds the dropped key, and beside it a long-lost earring.
proc: A small light reveals what was there all along.
A small light reveals something that lay there all along.

obraz: The geese feed with one head always raised.
proc: Watchful guarding while the rest feed.
One always keeps watch while the others feed.

obraz: The candle kept for a special evening has never been lit.
proc: Value left standing unused.
A thing of value is saved and never put to use.

obraz: The waterfall has become a wall of ice, its last streams held against the rock.
proc: What moved is stopped and held as it is.
Moving water has stopped and is held as it is.

obraz: Your foot finds the brake as the car ahead drifts, before you know why.
proc: Sensed and acted on before it can be explained.
The body senses the danger before it can be explained.

obraz: The new bulb in the hallway shows a crack that was always in the ceiling.
proc: A light shows something that was always there.
A light reveals what was there all along.

obraz: The cloud lifts, and you see how far up the slope you already are.
proc: Light clears and one sees where one stands.
Light returns and you see where you stand.

obraz: The battery you never use is flat on the day you need it.
proc: What stands unused loses its strength.
What is left unused loses its strength.

obraz: A chain of bubbles rises through the dark water, then stops beneath the clear ice.
proc: Movement stops and is held under the ice, in view.
Rising movement is halted and held under ice, visible in the stillness.

obraz: You turn back at the door, sure something is left behind, before you know what.
proc: Something sensed before it can be named.
Something is sensed before it can be named.

obraz: One match in the cave shows the wall an arm's length away and no further.
proc: A small flame reveals only a little.
A small flame reveals only what is close.

obraz: The low sun comes in under the cloud, and every stone on the moor has a shadow.
proc: The sun shines and everything shows where it stands.
Sunlight makes every single thing on the ground stand out.

obraz: The pool cut off from the river clouds over while the river runs clear.
proc: What stops moving spoils, what flows stays good.
What stands still spoils while what moves stays good.

obraz: A drop has frozen at the tip of an icicle, just before it falls.
proc: Movement stopped and held in one visible point.
A moving drop is stopped and held as it is.

obraz: The swell lifts the boat before any wave can be seen.
proc: A hidden current felt before anything is seen.
A hidden movement under the surface is felt before it is seen.

obraz: You bring a dish to the shared dinner and leave with a plate of someone else's cooking.
proc: Giving and receiving between sides, uncounted.
Something is given and something received between the sides, uncounted.

obraz: The sun comes round to the window, and every fingerprint on the glass shows.
proc: Sunlight shows everything, almost too much.
The sun simply shines and everything shows.

obraz: The lid holds, and holds, and gives under your grip.
proc: Resistance gives way to bodily strength.
Resistance gives way to the strength of the grip.

obraz: The lift stops between floors, and the building goes on humming around it.
proc: Something moving has stopped and is held.
Something moving has stopped and is held in place.

obraz: The dough rests under a tea towel, and by morning it has doubled.
proc: Covered and closed, it completes itself within.
Covered and left alone, it completes itself from within.

obraz: The borrowed book comes back with a bar of chocolate on top.
proc: A gift returned with a gift, not counted.
A gift goes one way and an uncounted thanks comes back.

obraz: Everyone agreed in the corridor; on the form there is one name, and it is yours.
proc: One person stands for the side taken and bears the cost alone.
Only you put your name down and carry the cost of the stand.

obraz: The salmon throws itself at the falls again.
proc: Raw bodily force thrown against resistance, repeatedly.
Raw bodily force is thrown against resistance.

obraz: The tree planted as a sapling beside the bench now shades the place where you sit.
proc: What was planted long ago shows its result in time.
What was planted long ago now gives its result.

obraz: The broken bone knits under the cast, and nothing can be seen of it.
proc: Completion within, nothing visible from outside.
Something completes itself inside while nothing shows outside.

obraz: Someone has remembered how you take your coffee.
proc: An attention given by one to another, uncounted.
A small uncounted attention passes from one person to another.

obraz: You tell the referee the ball was out, and your own team loses the point.
proc: Keeps to the truth and knowingly pays the price.
You take the honest side and pay the price knowingly.
